summary: The generator excludes the sourced ln(x)/4 family by rejecting unit-fraction coefficients. Sampled mathematics, native grading, rendering and packaging passed; no stored-pool defect was demonstrated.

source_analysis.skill: Differentiate a constant multiple of ln(x), preserving the whole signed constant, including rational constants and multiples of e.
reasoning_steps: Identify the constant factor, rewriting ln(x)/d as (1/d)ln(x) when needed.
Apply the constant multiple rule and d(ln x)/dx=1/x.
Simplify c/x and select the matching radio answer or enter an equivalent expression.
invariants: Single natural logarithm with argument x; no chain rule, sums, general bases or point evaluation.
Easy workload: one constant multiple derivative, optionally rewriting a quotient by a constant.
Radio banks have five alternatives; blank inputs must accept mathematically equivalent notation.
permitted_variations: Signed integer and modest rational coefficients; proper and improper fractions.
Integer multiples of the constant e.
Quotient presentation ln(x)/d and factor presentation c ln(x).
Radio option order and correct position are incidental; distractors should remain plausible and unique.
Changing the coefficient must change the answer; reordering choices must preserve its mathematical value.
source_refs: tutorial b1f46211-3766-53d0-bcc7-30bb9056b948: The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function; d(ln x)/dx=1/x.

packaging.details: Exact Python 3.13.5 and SymPy 1.14.0 dependencies match manifest. CLI reproduces the runner batch, relocated runtime reproduces it, no external assets are required, and package hashes remain unchanged.

decision_variation.details: Relevant coefficient changes and irrelevant seed changes behave correctly; tested position cues are not reliable. However the specification fixes multiplier presentation and excludes the source quotient-rewriting decision case. findings.description: Source q-70887 asks y=ln(x)/4 with answer 1/(4x), but generate_easy(parameters={n:1,d:4,k:0}) raises ValueError. validate_parameters requires |n|>=2 for every profile, and the template/bank inventory has no quotient-by-a-constant family. This removes a demonstrated easy reasoning case: rewrite division by a constant before applying the constant multiple rule.
